subject: NorthForge dedicated footprint & latency guarantee plan
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@northforge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — NorthForge inference traffic sample attached

Hi Irene / Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to understand what a Dedicated deployment would look like for our 'northforge-infer-v2' model if we move from 100k monthly requests to a production profile: steady daytime traffic with two short peaks per day (09:00 and 16:00 PST). Our primary constraint is p95 gen latency <= 300ms for single-turn text completion at 2k token prompts.

Attached is a small sample of our recent traffic (northforge-traffic-sample.csv). The key asks:
- Back-of-envelope tokens/sec estimate for our peak windows (we're seeing ~1,800 concurrent sessions at peak).
- How many GPUs (and which SKU) you'd recommend to hit p95 <= 300ms with a comfortable headroom for spiky load.
- Any fallback routing / degradation strategies if capacity is saturated.

Procurement is already expecting a capacity proposal — cc'd contracts@northforge.ai. Can you take a look and tell us what info you need to convert this into a formal Dedicated proposal?

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform
NorthForge AI

Attachment: northforge-traffic-sample.csv (CSV stub: timestamp, requests, avg_tokens_per_req)

Hi Evan — thanks for the sample. I pulled it in and had a quick pass. Two quick clarifying questions before we run an internal sizing:
1) Are the 1,800 concurrent sessions concurrent active in-flight requests, or session slots where only ~10% are sending live inference at any moment?
2) What latency SLO is firm (p95 <= 300ms is clear) and do you have a p50/p99 target for planning?

On the surface, with a 2k-token average prompt and the model description, I expect the model is in the 30–70B parameter class. That maps to a wide span of per-GPU tokens/sec depending on quantization and runtime. If you can confirm concurrency semantics I’ll loop in infra for a formal estimate and propose a reserve slab with headroom margin.

If helpful I can also do a quick back-of-envelope now with conservative assumptions to unblock procurement.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@northforge.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — NorthForge inference traffic sample attached

Hi all — I ran the sample through our quick-sizing heuristic and attached a compact workbook (karthik-tps-model.xlsx). Summary below (back-of-envelope; we should validate with a short perf run):

Assumptions we used:
- Model family: 35–70B dense transformer (northforge indicated model complexity).
- Runtime: optimized Redwood runtime with KV caching not applicable for single-turn completions.
- Target p95 <= 300ms observed at per-request generation of ~2k tokens (generation-only, excluding pre/post processing).
- Hardware options evaluated: A100-80 (single choice for initial Dedicated) and a 4-bit quantized variant if you opt-in to quantization testing later.

Estimated per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec) at target latency (p95 ~300ms):
- Conservative (35–40B, int8-like path): ~600–900 tokens/sec per GPU
- Conservative (60–70B, int8 path): ~250–420 tokens/sec per GPU

Traffic sizing mapping (peak):
- Peak concurrent active requests: 1,800 sessions, assume average generation overlap of 1.2s per 200 tokens -> translates to ~9k tokens/sec request aggregate (conservative).
- Using 600 tps (lower-end 35–40B) -> ~15 GPUs to meet nominal token rate.
- Using 300 tps (conservative 60–70B) -> ~30 GPUs.

Headroom & SLO mapping:
- We apply a 1.6x safety multiplier for burstiness (workloads with diurnal spikes) and 1.1x for ops margin -> overall multiplier ~1.8x.
- Recommended committed slab (initial):
  - If you can quantize / use 35–40B variant: commit 25 A100-80GB GPUs (gives ~15 * 1.8 ≈ 27 needed vs 25 recommended after negotiation on burst policy).
  - If you must run 60–70B dense: recommend 55 A100-80GB GPUs (30 * 1.8 ≈ 54).

Operational notes / fallback suggestions:
- Warm standby model variants: route low-priority requests to a smaller quantized variant automatically when average queue depth crosses threshold.
- Soft-throttle at ingress with 95th-percentile-banded routing (we will preserve p95 by shedding best-effort traffic).
- Prioritize canary route for new releases; rollback to smaller model variant if end-to-end latency goes above SLO.

Next steps I propose:
1) A 24h perf run using a 10% slice of your traffic (we can host in Dedicated dev slab) to measure real-world tokens/sec/latency.
2) We will run that perf, update the workbook, and deliver a committed slab proposal with cost delta between the two SKU scenarios.

Attachment: karthik-tps-model.xlsx (workbook: per-GPU tps curves, multiplier knobs, cost calc sheet)

- Karthik
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — NorthForge inference traffic sample attached

Quick addition to Karthik's excellent breakdown:
- For committed slabs we should include an automated fallback policy in the SLA addendum: when cluster CPU/GPU utilization > 78% for 5 minutes, an automatic route-level downgrade kicks in (route-level fallback to quantized variant). That reduces required committed GPUs by ~10% for most duty cycles and gives the customer a lower committed cost option.
- I'll draft the fallback wording for Contracts. Also suggest we include a short-run cost-protection credit if latency breaches p95 more than twice in a month during an onboarding window.

I'll coordinate the wording with Kimberly on procurement language.

— Priyom
Staff Product, Redwood Inference
